title: North American birds colonised climate-suitable survey routes only within about 100 km of occupied routes, and most climate-expected gains lay farther away (BBS 1981-2025)
abstract: Question: bird community temperature indices follow only a small part of their spatial temperature slope, and the gap is in species membership. Does colonist supply limit colonisation? Data: North American Breeding Bird Survey 2026 release, 1,680 routes, 306 species, 1981-95 versus 2011-25 (0.85 C warming), GHCN_CAMS temperature; UK Butterfly Monitoring Scheme as a replication. Method: cross-fitted temperature niche models gave suitability S and its climate-driven change dS. Linear probability models with species effects compared the temporal slope t on dS with the spatial slope g on S (R = t/g; 1 = full space-for-time response) for 268,508 absent and 118,464 occupied route-species pairs, by distance to the nearest occupied route; 2-degree block bootstrap; within-region warming placebo; an early interval with 0.32 C warming. Results: colonisation fell from 24% within 40 km of an occupied route to 0.2% beyond 300 km. R* was 0.74 (95% CI -0.03 to 1.61) within 40 km, 0.27 (0.01-0.59) at 40-100 km, 0.09 at 100-300 km and 0.01 beyond. Of the climate-expected colonisation gain, 61% lay beyond 300 km (29% inside species longitude bands); the median isotherm shift was 99 km. Persistence followed dS at R 0.93 (0.66-1.14), with no rescue effect. The placebo and the early interval showed that most of the dS slope is a warming-independent edge pattern. After this edge trend was absorbed, colonisation followed local warming at 0.98 (0.47-1.59) of g and regional warming at 0.73 (0.44-1.01); the edge trend nearly cancelled them. UK butterflies were uninformative. Conclusion: near sources, birds follow warming at about full strength; colonist supply beyond about 100 km limits community warming. Limitations: temperature-only niches, collinear edge and regional warming terms, detection changes, post-hoc distance classes.

Raw rates also differ in baseline suitability. (b) Share of absent pairs and of the climate-expected colonisation gain (g_A x positive dS) in each distance class, for all pairs and inside each species' longitude band.

Spatial slope g (open squares), temporal slope t on climate-driven suitability change dS (orange) and the mean placebo slope with warming permuted among routes in the same Bird Conservation Region (grey), by distance to the nearest occupied route. 95% intervals from a 200-draw 2-degree block bootstrap. (a) Colonisation; (b) persistence.

(a) Response to a niche-position index (niche slope x 0.85 C, the same scale in both intervals) relative to g, for 1966-80 to 1981-95 (0.32 C warming, blue) and 1981-95 to 2011-25 (0.85 C, orange). The edge pattern does not scale with warming. (b) Four-term model: warming-independent edge trend, response to Bird Conservation Region mean warming and to local warming deviations, each divided by g, all pairs. Dashed line: full space-for-time equivalence.
